analysis.title: Raymond James Investment Strategy daily, Monday, November 2, 2026 (Up and Adam)
key_insights: Hyperscaler capex scale and its drag on free cash flow drove last week's weakness in AI-related equities. Raymond James stays constructive on Technology because AI demand is accelerating: cloud revenue grew 63% YoY on average in 3Q26 versus 54% in 2Q, and backlogs rose 141% YoY to $1.8t.
The 10-year Treasury yield fell 35 bps in October, the largest monthly drop since February 2025. The Bloomberg Treasury Index gained 2.4%, its best month since December 2023.
Markets price two Fed rate hikes over the next 12 months, down from three a few weeks ago. Raymond James still expects only one hike and sees cooling inflation pulling the 10-year toward 4.50%-4.75%.
Bond investors are focused this week on the midterm elections and the Treasury's refunding announcement.

The S&P 500 fell 1.8% on Friday, its steepest drop since June 5, and closed below its 100-day moving average. Raymond James still expects ~19% S&P 500 EPS growth over the next 12 months and keeps an 8,450 index target, and recommends diversification and time in the market.

Since 1950, November and December have been the strongest two-month stretch for the S&P 500, averaging gains above 3% with positive returns 77% of the time. October was a counter-example, with the index down 0.9% against a long-term average gain of 0.9%.

Gold closed below $4,000/oz on Friday for the first time since July, its lowest close since October 2025. It fell ~7% in October while the 10-year yield also fell, so the usual inverse relationship between gold and yields has broken down. Raymond James calls gold a sentiment-driven commodity.
Pre-market on Nov 2, S&P 500 futures were up 0.4% and Nasdaq 100 futures up 0.8%. Today's releases are S&P Global Manufacturing PMI, Construction Spending and ISM Manufacturing.
